'''Roberto Daniele Peccei''' ({{IPA|it|petˈtʃɛi|lang}}; January 6, 1942<ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=allYAAAAMAAJ&q=Peccei,+ROberto+Daniele%22+AND+%221942%22 |title=American men & women of science: a ... - Google Books |date=2008-02-14 |publisher=R.R. Bowker |access-date=2011-10-07|isbn=9781414433059 }}</ref> – June 1, 2020)<ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-06-04|title=In memoria di Roberto Peccei|url=https://www.greenreport.it/news/in-memoria-di-roberto-peccei/|access-date=2020-06-05|website=Greenreport: economia ecologica e sviluppo sostenibile|language=it-IT|archive-date=2020-06-05|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200605051225/https://www.greenreport.it/news/in-memoria-di-roberto-peccei/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|url=https://clubofrome.org/impact-hubs/climate-emergency/roberto-peccei-in-memoriam/ |title=In Memoriam |publisher= Club of Rome |date=2020-06-01 |access-date=2020-06-01}}</ref> was a theoretical particle physicist whose principal interests lay in the area of [[electroweak]] interactions and in the interface between [[particle physics]] and [[physical cosmology]]. He was most known for formulating the [[Peccei–Quinn theory]] (with [[Helen Quinn]]), which attempts to resolve the [[strong CP problem]] in particle physics.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Peccei|first1=R. D.|last2=Quinn|first2=Helen R.|date=1977|title=CP Conservation in the Presence of Pseudoparticles|journal=Physical Review Letters|language=en|volume=38|issue=25|pages=1440–1443|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.38.1440|bibcode=1977PhRvL..38.1440P|issn=0031-9007}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Peccei|first1=R. D.|last2=Quinn|first2=Helen R.|date=1977|title=Constraints imposed by CP conservation in the presence of pseudoparticles|journal=Physical Review D|language=en|volume=16|issue=6|pages=1791–1797|doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.16.1791|bibcode=1977PhRvD..16.1791P|issn=0556-2821}}</ref>

Peccei was a vice chancellor for research at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] between 2000 and 2010.

==Early life and education==
The son of [[Aurelio Peccei]] (founder of the [[Club of Rome]]), Roberto Peccei was born in 1942 in [[Torino, Italy]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=In memoriam: Roberto Peccei, 78, internationally renowned particle physicist|url=https://newsroom.ucla.edu/stories/in-memoriam-roberto-peccei-78-internationally-renowned-particle-physicist|access-date=2020-06-13|website=UCLA|language=en-US}}</ref> He completed his secondary school in [[Argentina]], and came to the [[United States]] in 1958 to pursue his university studies in physics. He obtained a B.S. from [[MIT]] in 1962, and M.S. from [[New York University]] (NYU) in 1964 and a Ph.D. from the [[MIT Center for Theoretical Physics]] in 1969.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=94640|title=Robert D. Peccei}}</ref>

==Career==
After a brief period of postdoctoral work at the [[University of Washington]], he joined the faculty of [[Stanford University]] in 1971, where (with [[Helen Quinn]]) he originated [[Peccei–Quinn theory]], still the most famous proposed solution to the [[strong CP problem]].<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{cite arXiv|eprint=hep-ph/0011376|author=Dine, Michael|title=TASI Lectures on The Strong CP Problem|year=2000 }}</ref><ref>{{cite book|author=Peccei, R.D.|year=2008|chapter=The Strong CP Problem and Axions|title=Axions|series=Lecture Notes in Physics|volume=741|pages=3–17|arxiv=hep-ph/0607268|bibcode=2008LNP...741....3P|doi=10.1007/978-3-540-73518-2_1|isbn=978-3-540-73517-5|s2cid=119482294 }}</ref> In 1978, he returned to Europe as a staff member of the [[Max Planck Institute]] in [[Munich]], [[Germany]]. He joined the ''Deutsches Elektronen-Synchrotron'' ([[DESY]]) Laboratory in [[Hamburg]], Germany, as the head of the Theoretical Group in 1984. He returned to the United States in 1989, joining the faculty of the Department of Physics at [[UCLA]]. Soon thereafter, he became chair of the department, a position he held until becoming dean of the division of physical sciences of the College of Letters and Sciences in 1993.<ref name=":0" />

Until his death in June 2020, Peccei was on the editorial board of ''Nuclear Physics B Supplement'', and the ''Journal of Physics G''.{{cn|date=June 2020}} He was a member of the [[Club of Rome]], a trustee of the [[World Academy of Art and Science]] and president of the Fondazione Aurelio Peccei and he was a Fellow of both the [[American Physical Society]] and the [[Institute of Physics]] in the [[United Kingdom]]. In the last 15 years, he served on numerous advisory boards both in Europe and in the U.S. He chaired both the scientific advisory board for the Laboratory for Nuclear Science at [[Cornell University]] and the visiting committee for the Laboratory of Nuclear Science at MIT. He also was a member of the visiting committee for the Department of Physics at MIT and was the convener of the vice chancellor for Research Council in the University of California.{{cn|date=June 2020}}
